row.evidence: Amazon Redshift manages workforce access "through trusted-identity propagation" from AWS IAM Identity Center and creates users on first login, but "the user is not automatically deleted from the Amazon Redshift catalog" when removed from the IdP; there is no SCIM endpoint.
row.notes: Amazon Redshift is usage-priced (Provisioned from $0.543/hour, Serverless from $1.50/hour), so seat and SCIM price fields are empty. There is no SCIM endpoint into Redshift: identities come from AWS IAM Identity Center (which itself accepts SCIM from Okta, Entra ID and others) via trusted identity propagation, from native IdP federation (Entra ID, users created on first login with groups mapped to roles), or from IAM federation with GetClusterCredentials AutoCreate. Deleting a user in Identity Center or the IdP does not remove the Redshift user; admins must run DROP USER. Database users are otherwise managed with SQL (CREATE/ALTER/DROP USER). Identity Center's own SCIM belongs to the AWS row, not this one. 'None' is by absence (rule 5).

plans.name: Redshift Provisioned
plans.notes: Hourly node pricing; reserved instances available.

limitations.text: Users removed from IAM Identity Center or the connected IdP are not deleted from the Redshift catalog; an admin must run DROP USER.

scim.notes: Redshift has no SCIM endpoint. Workforce identities reach it through AWS IAM Identity Center (which an IdP can provision over SCIM) and trusted identity propagation, through native IdP federation (Entra ID), or through IAM federation with auto-created database users. 'false' is by absence (rule 5): the Redshift Management Guide and Database Developer Guide document no SCIM service.

capabilities.notes: invite_user and assign_licenses false: Redshift has database users, no invitations or licences.

endpoints.path: CREATE USER name [ WITH ] PASSWORD { 'password' | 'md5hash' | 'sha256hash' | DISABLE } [ option [ ... ] ]

endpoints.purpose: Change a database user (rename, password, expiry, connection limit, session timeout)
Drop one or more database users
Issue temporary database credentials; AutoCreate=true creates the user (sample request is a query-string call)

user_api.notes: Database users are managed with SQL DDL (CREATE USER, ALTER USER, DROP USER), run by a superuser or a user with the matching privilege; the Redshift Data API can run these statements over HTTPS. The management API action GetClusterCredentials can auto-create a database user (AutoCreate=true) and issue temporary credentials.

okta.notes: No Redshift app in the Okta OIN (okta.com/integrations/amazon-redshift/ and /aws-redshift/ return 404); Okta reaches Redshift through IAM Identity Center or AWS IAM federation.

entra.notes: Native IdP federation supports Entra ID (Azure AD) tokens with JIT users and group-to-role mapping; no Entra gallery provisioning app checked.

fallbacks.other_sync: AWS IAM Identity Center trusted identity propagation (Identity Center holds the users and groups, e.g. provisioned from Okta or Entra ID)
fallbacks.notes: JIT: native IdP federation (OAuth tokens from Entra ID) creates the user and maps groups to roles on login; IAM/SAML federation via GetClusterCredentials AutoCreate creates the database user. csv_import false: not applicable to a database.
